'''Michèle Leduc''' (born 1942){{r|idref}} is a retired French physicist known for her research on the development of [[infrared]] [[laser]]s, their application in [[optical pumping]] and [[hyperpolarized gas MRI]], and for leading early observations of [[Bose–Einstein condensate]]s of [[helium]].{{r|atominnen}} She is an [[professor emeritus|emerita]] director of research for the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS), affiliated with the Bose–Einstein condensate team of the [[Kastler–Brossel Laboratory]] of CNRS and the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)]],{{r|lkb}} and a former president of the [[Société Française de Physique]].{{r|pres-sfp}}

==Education and career==
Leduc became a student at the [[École normale supérieure de jeunes filles]] in 1961, and received an [[agrégation]] in physical sciences in 1965. She completed a [[doctorat d'état]] in 1972, through the [[University of Paris]].{{r|lkb}}

She joined the CNRS in 1969, as a researcher in the Laboratoire de spectroscopie hertzienne, which later became the Kastler–Brossel Laboratory.{{r|lkb}} She became part of a group with [[Claude Cohen-Tannoudji]] studying ultracold atoms in the 1990s; Cohen-Tannoudji received the Nobel prize in 1997 for his group's research.{{r|atominnen}} In 2001, a team led by Leduc and Cohen-Tannoudji became one of two groups to make the first observations of helium Bose–Einstein condensates.{{r|helium}}

She directed the Center for Physics of the [[Les Houches School of Physics]] from 1993 to 1998, and directed the Kastler–Brossel Laboratory from 1994 to 1999.{{r|lkb}} By 2005, she had become a director of research (exceptional class) for the CNRS. She retired as a director of research emerita in 2007.{{r|lkb}}

From 2007 to 2008, and again for an interim term in 2009, she was president of the Société Française de Physique.{{r|pres-sfp}} She directed the Institut francilien de recherche sur les atomes froids from 2005 to 2012, and chaired the ethics committee of the CNRS from 2012 to 2016.{{r|lkb}}

==Recognition==
Leduc received the [[Prix Paul Doistau–Émile Blutet]] in the physical sciences in 1976. She was the 1989 recipient of the {{ill|Prix Science et Défense|fr}} of the [[Direction générale de l'armement]], and one of four 1998 recipients of the [[Körber European Science Prize]].{{r|lkb}} In 2009, she received the [[Irène Joliot-Curie Prize]] as female scientist of the year.{{r|ijc}}

She was named as a knight in the [[Ordre des Arts et des Lettres]] in 1987, as a commander in the [[Ordre national du Mérite]] in 2010, and as a commander in the [[Legion of Honour]] in 2014.{{r|lkb}}
